# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter,
**_Fox News_ shifted their rating of the Texas governor’s race for the second time in a month.**
[****](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260929_1_powerrankings.ffASVT&refcode=em20260929-2263&amount=5&t=1&akid=2263%2E299639%2E2qGNU_)
Seven weeks ago, _Fox News_ had our race as “Solid Republican.” Six weeks ago, they moved it to “Likely Republican.” And recently, they graded our race as “Lean Republican.”
Fox wrote that Texas is “drifting away” from the GOP. They’ve woken up to what our campaign has known for months: Texans are ready for change, and they’re ready for an end to Greg Abbott’s corruption.
Greg Abbott has spent this campaign defending data center deals that are driving up electricity costs and water use across the state, while our campaign is holding him accountable.
Last week, with the race clearly tightening, Abbott hit the panic button — halting new data center construction until at least December, _after the election_.
He knows voters are paying attention. He’s just too late.
Abbott still has structural advantages, like the $67 million war chest he’s sitting on, which he’s already started spending to attack us. That’s why we need all hands on deck to make sure this race keeps moving in our direction.

---

For the past few weeks, my life has resembled George Clooney's character in _Up in the Air_ -- the 2009 film where he's living out of airports, speaking at a different conference every day. Genine Fallon was there too every step of the way (You can subscribe to her new substack [here](https://substack.com/@g9fallon).)
Much of our trip centered on 'veterpreneurship' -- helping more veterans become founders, owners, investors, and business leaders.
Our first stop was Jackson Hole for the [Wyoming Global Tech Summit](https://substack.com/redirect/f48147a3-80c3-4ba6-90b5-729b5845f67f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). We quickly understood why people make the trip. The caliber of people in the room and the depth of the conversations around defense technology, AI, robotics, and public-private partnerships were extraordinary. It reinforced just how much innovation is happening beyond the traditional technology hubs and the importance of connecting these communities.
That conversation continued at a dinner hosted by [Playground Global](https://substack.com/redirect/ef82596a-23cb-4edc-9d31-5ce4ca7b6df0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a Palo Alto venture firm that backs early-stage deep-tech companies working on some of the hardest problems in computing, AI, automation, and energy, where quantum technology and defense took center stage.
At an Amazon Ventures dinner in DC, we explored defense technology, AI, and the role of public-private partnerships in bringing emerging technologies to market. These conversations highlighted the importance of connecting entrepreneurs building breakthrough technologies with the investors and institutions capable of helping them scale.
At [SuperReturn US West](https://substack.com/redirect/796fa1d9-5222-4509-9fe1-8ac88bc64f99?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in Los Angeles, it was about how geopolitics, AI, supply chains, and national security are reshaping the global investment landscape. In Chicago, we continued that discussion with business leaders focused on navigating uncertainty, building resilient companies, and strengthening American competitiveness.
In Columbus, Ohio, I was proud to lead a bipartisan panel at the E[nergy Affordability Summit](https://substack.com/redirect/ee90feaf-dcd0-4e78-b26d-50d57c2c48fe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) with four U.S. senators, a governor, and business leaders focused on an 'abundance agenda' -- how we can make housing and energy more affordable through permitting reform. I recently made that case in the _[Washington Examiner](https://substack.com/redirect/c468e36f-365b-40d2-a5e4-4c847bb7f34e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_ with my fellow Iraq War veteran and former congressional colleague Steve Stivers, who now leads the Ohio Chamber of Commerce.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/658a5334-2b7e-4898-9942-68a5421497ec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
[](https://substack.com/redirect/d279bf9f-e977-49f2-9987-3c86149b7709?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
It was then back to Washington for the [Milken Institute](https://substack.com/redirect/472f3401-b6bf-447d-9dbd-93c68a2f6079?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s The Next Mission: Health, Capital, and Continued Service convening. The patriots in the room are working to advance conversations around veteran transitions, entrepreneurship, and access to capital. I moderated a discussion about connecting veterans with the resources, investment, and partnerships that can help them succeed long after their military service.
At the [Military Influencer Conference](https://substack.com/redirect/03f68893-d6b8-4470-acd4-c23d115041f7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in Tampa, we carried that conversation forward with a panel called From Service to Ownership: Veterans, Entrepreneurship, and the Ownership Economy, exploring how veterans can build, buy, and lead the next generation of American businesses with the Silver Tsnumi coming - the majority of the 36 million small businesses are led by someone over 55 years old and don't have a succession plan.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5bcb9455-64b0-41c1-a98f-396e946dabcf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
We owe a special thank you to the teams at all these conferences for bringing together such remarkable people and advancing these important conversations.
The real work is connecting the people, capital, and innovation driving America's future with action plans so these aren't just academic exercises. The relationships we're building are just as important as the conversations themselves, and we're excited to keep moving this work forward.
The next mission isn't just about what America can do for veterans. It's about what veterans can do for America.
Sprinkled in with national television hits on CNN, Bloomberg and a clip here on BBC where we talk about the 'whole of nation' approach to some of our greatest challenges (not just 'whole of government').
[](https://substack.com/redirect/ead5f45e-9398-4bce-a229-ef2c5255f768?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Next stops: AUSA in Washington, DC, October 12-15, and DAV Bootcamp in Cincinnati, October 20-21\. If you happen to be attending, be sure to say hi and let us know if you'd like to be part of the solution with this next mission.

body:
Eugene Vindman needs your support.

**🇺🇸 To all supporters of Eugene Vindman: Please don’t ignore this message. Our final quarterly FEC deadline is tomorrow night and we are short of where we need to be. ⛅**
Eugene has devoted his life to serving our country: in the Army, the National Security Council, and now as a member of Congress.
But he’s up for re-election against a formidable MAGA opponent who is _attacking him relentlessly._ He’s launched attack ads against him, and even a website dedicated to smearing his record.

Eugene is already a top target for Trump after blowing the whistle on him 7 years ago, and recently calling on Trump to release questionable call transcripts with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman. And his race is one of the most competitive races in the country.
So we have no doubt that Eugene will continue to be subjected to limitless attacks by his opponent, Donald Trump, and National Republicans.

**Peter, if we don't have the resources to fight back against these attacks, we could lose this seat.** But to win, it's going to take resources — resources that only this grassroots team can help us build.
But truthfully, we’re seeing a major slowdown in our fundraising, and the timing couldn't be worse as we **our final quarterly FEC deadline ends tomorrow night!**
The strength of this campaign has always come from people like you who chip in what they can, when they can. Our average online donation is about $27. Some give more, many give less. What matters is that people give to support Eugene when they can. Especially during a critical moment like this one.

So we’re asking:
[**Peter, if you can, please contribute $3 before our FEC deadline ends to help ensure Eugene has the resources to fight back against the attacks and win this race. name: Eric Pratt
subject: A quick personal note from Prior Lake
body:
With voting underway, our team needs a boost to finish September strong.

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/NbOlWGTdiYQ?e=905d578f8e&c2id=16eb929e7cba591464984f29a5a61342)
| | | | | | ,

Hard to believe it, but we are just a little over a month away from Election Day. Ballots are officially moving, early voting is underway, and folks across Dakota, Scott, Rice, Washington, and Le Sueur counties are already making their voices heard.
---
| [VOTING IS UNDERWAY — HELP US REACH MN-02 VOTERS >>](https://us.list-manage.com/nzj7Pqm3a64?e=905d578f8e&c2id=16eb929e7cba591464984f29a5a61342)
---
| | | | | | | | | | | |

I’ve lived in Prior Lake since the 1970s. My mother taught in Shakopee for 25 years, Tina and I raised our kids here, and I spent my career in business before serving on our local school board. I love this district—and I know the folks who live here expect practical, common-sense leadership that balances the budget and respects the hard-working taxpayer.We don't rely on D.C. political action committees or out-of-state dark money to fund our work. This campaign is built from the ground up by neighbors, friends, and local families who just want to see good, honest accountability brought back to government.As we wrap up the month of September, our team faces our most important fundraising deadline yet.The radical left is spending heavily to protect their allies in Minnesota, and if we are going to keep our door-knockers on the pavement, keep our signs up, and get our common-sense message to every voter before they fill out their ballot, I need to ask for your help today.
---
| [WILL YOU CHIP IN $15, $25, OR $50 BEFORE OUR MIDNIGHT EOM DEADLINE? >>](https://us.list-manage.com/kumTrCDd7bz?e=905d578f8e&c2id=16eb929e7cba591464984f29a5a61342)
---
| |

If you're able to help us finish September strong with a grassroots gift today, it would mean the world to me and our entire team.Thank you for your neighborly encouragement, your prayers, and for taking the field with us.Warmly,Eric PrattCandidate for U.S. Congress (MN-02)
---
|
---

name: Roy Cooper
subject: You've caught my eye
body:
I’m not reaching out to everyone today – just a select few, including you.
| [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1370&source=&t=1&akid=4005%2E124072%2EPU5UFc) | | | |
---
Peter, I’m not reaching out to everyone today – just a select few, including you.
My team was going through our supporter records, and we noticed how yours stood out from the crowd. You’re one of my most attentive grassroots supporters. You’ve been getting these emails for a while now, and we see you're keeping up with the latest on this election. I want you to know that _I know_ how engaged you’ve been with our campaign and how much I appreciate it.
**Today, I’m asking you to take the next step. Here's why:**
Grassroots fundraising has really slowed down these last few weeks, and it couldn’t come at a worse time. Republican super PACs have already been pouring just over $100 million so far into North Carolina to defeat me, and now, a super PAC aligned with President Trump is unleashing millions more to double down on their attacks.
Since recent polls show this race statistically tied, we need to turn this around fast – and the first step is reaching our $5 million end-of-quarter goal before our last quarterly FEC deadline tomorrow night. [**_Will you chip in $5 right now to help us get there in time? The stakes could not be higher._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1370&amount=5&t=8&akid=4005%2E124072%2EPU5UFc)
North Carolina is the best chance Democrats have to flip one of the four seats we need to take back the Senate, so if we lose here, we lose our shot at flipping the majority. The only way we’ll avoid that is by building the resources to compete with the massive amounts of GOP spending.
**Unlike my MAGA opponent Michael Whatley, I’m not a Washington DC insider who can rely on his billionaire connections to buy this Senate seat. I’m depending on people like you, giving what you can, when you can, at crucial moments like this.**
_With a little more than 24 hours to close the gap, Peter, I need you._
[**_Time’s running out, so I’m personally asking: Will you please chip in your first $5 donation to my campaign today so we can reach our ambitious end-of-quarter goal before the FEC deadline tomorrow, flip North Carolina’s critical seat and help Democrats secure the Senate majority?_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1370&amount=5&t=9&akid=4005%2E124072%2EPU5UFc)

| | | | JoCasta Zamarripa is a lifelong Milwaukeean, a proud daughter of the city’s south side, and a dedicated public servant who’s never stopped fighting for working people. Born and raised in the very neighborhoods she now represents, JoCasta has spent her life pushing for progress that reflects the realities of everyday Wisconsinites.

[ ](https://us.list-manage.com/bigR61d1aSu?e=8d919f2092&c2id=0bdcb6d83cbc8b2aaf05afb952b88bb7)

She made history as the first Latina and first openly bi member of both the Wisconsin State Legislature and the Milwaukee Common Council. But JoCasta’s leadership is defined by more than her historic firsts—it's grounded in results. She served ten years in the State Assembly and is now in her second term as Alderperson for Milwaukee’s 8th District, where she’s led major efforts on affordable housing, small business licensing reform, and community development.

In 2025, she was the lead sponsor of the Housing Element Plan, a key step in addressing Milwaukee’s housing crisis by expanding affordable options and preventing displacement. Her approach is practical and persistent—building coalitions, navigating political challenges, and staying rooted in the neighborhoods she serves.

Now, JoCasta is running as a Democrat for Wisconsin Secretary of State to use the platform to fight for what matters: more funding for our schools so families aren’t forced into referenda every election, real housing relief for working people, and affordable child care that lets parents breathe.

name: Gabby Giffords
subject: Aphasia makes it harder for me to speak
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Giffords PAC; not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee
body:
But I have not lost my voice.
#

Friend
Fifteen years ago, a gunman shot me in the head while I was meeting with constituents in front of a grocery store in Tucson.
[](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giff-em-q32026.gsDos-&refcode=em260929-1-b&t=1&akid=11877%2E3935704%2EwO3Uqu)
The bullet damaged the left hemisphere of my brain, where the language function sits. Ever since, aphasia has been a part of my life. This means that even though the words are in my head, I have a hard time getting them out.
**Aphasia may make it harder for me to speak. But I have not lost my voice.**
[](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giff-em-q32026.gsDos-&refcode=em260929-1-b&t=2&akid=11877%2E3935704%2EwO3Uqu)
The road to recovery hasn’t been easy, but I’ve never given up. In addition to speech therapy and physical therapy, I dedicate much of my time to riding my bike, playing my French horn, and practicing yoga. These activities have helped me so much in my recovery journey.
[](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giff-em-q32026.gsDos-&refcode=em260929-1-b&t=3&akid=11877%2E3935704%2EwO3Uqu)
I know the challenge of ending gun violence in our nation can feel overwhelming. When we see the headlines after a mass shooting, or when we remember the countless tragedies that don’t make the news every day, I know how hard it can be.
But friends, we cannot give up. I have found my recovery journey and the fight to end gun violence to be very similar. **Even on the hardest days, we can never lose hope.**
We are officially less than 48 hours away from our end-of-quarter FEC deadline. This final FEC fundraising deadline is a critical test for the gun safety movement, as both our adversaries and our allies will be looking to see if we have the resources to take on the gun lobby in November.
So this is where I need to ask for your help:
**[Will you make one last contribution of $3 to GIFFORDS PAC before our FEC deadline ends? We can’t reach our quarterly fundraising goals without your help.**](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giff-em-q32026.gsDos-&refcode=em260929-1-b&t=4&akid=11877%2E3935704%2EwO3Uqu)

It is when you arrive that you recall you cannot recall.
Not the turns--left or right.
Not the lights--stop, go, or slow.
Not even the exit.
The rhythmic blink of a turn signal, the steady hum of tires, the execution of a journey--a blur of motion without memory.
The miles are a void: a surrender to the drift.
It is always at least mildly disturbing.
And I recall Hillel:
"If I am not for myself, who will be for me? But if I am only for myself, who am I? If not now, when?"
**Pause.
Breath.
Look Deeper.**
**Refuel.**
**Welcome to Sweet Ground.**

Digital ads are one of the main ways we build and sustain this grassroots campaign. They let us reach voters, donors and concerned North Carolinians in every corner of the state. These ads are one of our most effective tools for mobilizing volunteers and keeping our grassroots fundraising going.
That's why this weekend's setback was such a big deal.
Because of a strange technical glitch that was not caused by us, our Facebook ads suddenly went dark, and we weren't able to run them all weekend. That's _two critical days_ of voter outreach gone. It may not sound like a big deal, but with only 35 days left in the campaign, we can't afford to lose a single second.
You may not have noticed the glitch, but it has put us in a tight spot. Here's why.
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/a9aaa383-80ac-4bac-9737-ff10abb85a57?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
**The outage cost us voter contact.**
The clock is running out on this campaign. Folks across the state are already sending back their absentee ballots, and they'll begin voting in person in about two weeks. (Thursday, October 15 to be exact).
I've been on the campaign trail, hosting Make Stuff Cost Less events, launching canvasses and hearing from voters all across the state. But as much as I wish I could, I can't be everywhere at once. So these ads are a critical opportunity for us to keep reaching voters and getting our message across, especially with such little time left.
**Our end-of-quarter deadline is tomorrow.**
In about 36 hours, we'll close the books on the most important fundraising report of this campaign. It will show just how strong our grassroots movement is, and everyone will be able to see it: journalists, supporters and opponents alike. A strong showing proves what we've known all along: North Carolinians are ready for a change and they're tired of the corruption coming out of Washington DC.
But we lost two days of fundraising, and have to make up the hundreds of thousands of dollars lost before tomorrow night.
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/a9aaa383-80ac-4bac-9737-ff10abb85a57?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
**And we can 't afford to fall behind.**
After two recent Supreme Court decisions made it easier for my opponent to be bankrolled by GOP dark money super PACs, they're spending over **$100 million** against me. So we can't afford to lose any part of our mobilization strategy. Not even for two days, and certainly not this close to Election Day.
**Will you help us get back on track?**
This race was always going to be won by out-organizing and out-communicating our opponent with the help of our grassroots supporters. Now, we're in a deficit, working to make up for lost outreach and hit our end-of-quarter fundraising goal.
[Will you chip in $5 or whatever you can spare to help us close the gap, flip North Carolina blue and take back the Senate?](https://substack.com/redirect/a9aaa383-80ac-4bac-9737-ff10abb85a57?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

Thank you. Whether you've donated, knocked on a door, shared a post, or simply believed in what we're building together, you are the reason this campaign is strong. I don't take a single bit of that for granted.
Today I'm reaching out because we've reached a moment that will shape the rest of this race, and I need your help.
**Our quarterly reporting deadline is Wednesday, September 30, at midnight, and we need to raise $6,000 before it closes.**
Here's why this deadline matters so much:
* **It keeps our digital ads running.** In the final stretch, our ads are how we reach thousands of voters in Butler, Preble, Darke, and Mercer Counties who haven't heard our message yet. Every dollar you give helps us meet people where they are, on their phones and in their feeds.
* **It keeps us on the Democratic slate card.** The slate card is one of the most trusted tools voters use when they head to the polls. We must meet our fundraising commitment to keep our place on it. Losing that spot would make it harder for voters to find us at the exact moment they're making their decision.

**Here's how we get there, together:** ✅ **60 people giving $100** , or
✅ **100 people giving $60**
That's it. That's all it takes. When neighbors come together, big goals become very reachable.****

#### **Forward Party Endorses Independent Congressional Candidate Rep. Kevin Kiley in California's Newly Drawn 6th District**
**_Washington D.C. – September 29, 2026_** _–_ The Forward Party recently announced its endorsement of Independent Rep. Kevin Kiley, who is seeking reelection to represent California's newly drawn 6th Congressional District in the November general election, continuing the party's support for candidates who put constituents ahead of party loyalty. Kiley currently serves as the sole Independent member of the U.S. House of Representatives, a distinction that reflects his consistent record of working across party lines rather than toward any single party's agenda. Kiley left the Republican party earlier this year after _**denouncing**_ the partisan redistricting efforts that took place both in his home state of California and other states across the country. He has become the only sitting independent in Congress and is now looking to prove that success outside the two-party system is viable. Kiley is a rare voice in the House who has consistently called out dysfunction in both parties, pushing for independent representation that breaks institutional gridlock. After being impacted by mid-decade redistricting, Kiley introduced legislation to ban the practice earlier this year. [_Read the full press announcement_](https://www.forwardparty.com/media/press_release/forward-party-endorses-independent-congressional-candidate-rep-kevin-kiley-in-californias-newly-drawn-6th-district/?e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_124a&n=1) _._ _**And that's not all...**_ **California’s 24th Congressional District Candidate, Bob Smith, Changes Political Status to Independent****** Bob Smith, a Forward Party-backed congressional candidate running in California’s 24th District for a U.S. House seat recently changed his party status from Republican to Independent. **** Bob explained the move to a local news crew stating: **** "I've realized the diverse interests that we have here on the Central Coast from the fishing communities in Morro Bay to the ag communities in North County, down to our cities down here," said Smith. "We need somebody who's going to represent the Central Coast first and not political party affiliation."****[_Watch Smith sign for his political independence_](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=BL77plytbQ_Uv-89HaxxcY1OHNEUl3c9IriJWzq6sqIrQOi0ltVyOcqJ12t33tbCZeNfhXL2TDJV4xbhNFeTlJ_i2UtTnXcKv3dOzB6sV1dblnJ0hcSJF5KtnvvIMHg-DH-F7jcKtSu2esX9OnRgHw&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_124a&n=2) _._

From the Bezos money surge to Biden's border crisis, I've made it my mission to remain firm on the strong Texan values that not only keep our citizens free and safe, but make this state the greatest in the union. But I have to be honest with you: this fight feels different. Democrats are doing more than just running a campaign this cycle. People ask me all the time why I left the Republican Party. They expect a simple answer. A single moment. A breaking point. There wasn't one. There were _hundreds._ I grew up believing the GOP stood for something. Fiscal discipline. Strong institutions. A belief that character counted, that the office was bigger than the man who held it. That's the party my parents raised me to respect.That party is gone. What's left is a party that no longer asks whether something is true, only whether it's loyal. A party where senators who once criticized Donald Trump in private now defend him in public because they're afraid of a primary. A party that has traded the Constitution for a cult of personality. I sat in rooms with these people. I watched the transformation happen in real time — principle by principle, surrender by surrender. This is not the party of my father, who believed in hard work and honest leaders. It is not even the party it was ten years ago. **It is Donald Trump's party now, full stop. Derek, I was on the road this month as we kicked off early voting in Virginia and here’s a question I kept getting: Why is the president more focused on naming monuments after himself than he is on governing? **Seriously, the president even threatened to shut down the Kennedy Center just because he’s not allowed to put his name on it.** Never in my lifetime did I think we’d see this kind of CRAP from the President of the United States. And – even more disappointing to me – we’ve seen far too many Republicans in Congress cave to his every demand. A disabled Maine man died on his bedroom floor after workers at a Brewer autism group home gave him pancakes and allowed him to eat alone despite an eating disorder that caused severe choking risk.
His name was Justin King, and he was a ward of the state. He had no family to inspect the unlicensed We Care Residential Services facility in which Maine's Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) placed him.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f2eb6a7d-306a-46af-b5a2-010632aa6838?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Justin A. King (Source: Legacy.com)
That was Sept. 15, 2024 -- two days after state records reveal two We Care employees were arrested at the same home for assaulting a disabled resident.
Brewer Police investigating the man's death were so alarmed by the negligence and incompetence displayed by the Medicaid provider that one officer contacted Adult Protective Services, the office of state government responsible for protecting adults from abuse and neglect. The officer, according to his incident report, had no faith in the health care workers' ability to care for the other adult patient in the 15 Autumn Lane home.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/caf3d4a4-a208-4db2-9900-ce17dab9ff28?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
"I contacted Adult Protective Services regarding [the surviving patient's] wellbeing," the officer wrote. "I do not feel staff possess the skills to care for disabled individuals as they let [the deceased] who had a known eating disorder, eat by himself in his bedroom."
King was carted off to a funeral home and later laid to rest at a cemetery in Houlton, where he'd graduated from high school in 2000.
According to his obituary, King loved the outdoors, fishing, and was known throughout Houlton for his quirky sense of humor.
In the same year that We Care employees assaulted a disabled resident and King died in their custody, the autism company made $1.8 million through MaineCare Section 21, according to state payment records. The following year, the company earned $4.5 million.
MaineCare Section 21 is Maine's most expensive Medicaid program. It's designed to provide 24/7 care for Maine's most high-need and vulnerable adults, including adults with Autism Spectrum Disorder or Intellectual and Development Disorders. Although the number of Mainers receiving Section 21 care has remained steady in recent years, costs for the program have skyrocketed.
Sign up for The Robinson Report to support investigative journalism in Maine.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..szBmXQhIoVeLAz2sPRnhyYIlQ8OrKvFbRQdT5Ya0PHE?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=217846703)
Despite the sensitive nature of the work, the barriers to entry for new companies looking to tap into a virtually unlimited pool of Medicaid money are low.
According to state records, We Care CEO Francois Rukumbuzi incorporated his autism company in 2022 and began billing MaineCare in 2024. According to federal court records, Rukumbuzi is a native of the Democratic Republic of Congo who applied for asylum status in August 2016 and arrived in Maine by way of North Carolina.
Rukumbuzi's asylum suit does not identify a ground under the asylum statute, i.e. persecution due to race, religion, nationality, political opinion, or particular social group, and it does not describe any past harm, actor, or event. Instead, the court filing related to his asylum claim states that he fears returning to the DRC, "where he will certainly be persecuted, tortured, and/or killed."

Under the terms of that loan Rukumbuzi and Ndutira agreed to occupy the home for a period of one year, but they instead appear to have turned it into an income-generating residential care facility. _(FHA Case Number 231-1782371-703 / Loan No. 304-1006380 / Guild Mortgage Company LLC)_
Rather than occupying the autism group home, the couple lived in Westbrook and later Windham, according to public records.
That means Rukumbuzi and Ndutira misled the FHA and the bank to secure a low-interest loan for a property that immediately became a small business, rented back to the government-funded autism company Rukumbuzi started with the help of several other Central African migrants.

Records from the National Provider Index, a database of providers maintained by the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid (CMS), show the authorized official for We Care is also Mucyo.
CMS records show that Mucyo is the authorized official for Safe Haven Residential Care in Bismarck, N.D., a residential care company formed in January. Mucyo formed the North Dakota-based Medicaid business around the time he terminated Bridgeway Treatment Center LLC, a Medicaid-funded drug treatment business he incorporated in 2023, along with Rugumanya Murama, in Tucson, Arizona.
According to Brewer Police Department records, neither Mucyo nor Rukumbuzi were present in Brewer when the We Care client choked to death. Police records show the those Direct Support Professionals on site were Jonathan Nduwayo, Moses Tumusiime, and Modest Irakiza, and they were employees of We Care.

Peter Mutima and operated by his half-brother Felix Mutunzi, Safe Residential care billed the state of Maine more than $28 million to MaineCare in 2024.

King's choking death is just one example of the shocking negligence displayed by We Care and its employees, as well as the banal disregard and lack of effective policy enforcement from the DHHS under both former Commissioner Jeanne Lambrew and current Commissioner Sarah Gagne-Holmes. In addition to the choking death, state records show Maine health officials documented staff arrests, missing background checks, and what they concluded were falsified training credentials.
Many of these glaring violations of state law and MaineCare policies were documented several months or even years before the state took action.
Hanging over all of the egregious violations committed by We Care and its staff is a singular question: Why did the State wait so long to shut down the autism group home operator despite the obvious threat to the health and safety of disabled Mainers?
The state failures and grotesque abuses of human rights are documented in letters provided by DHHS in response to a Freedom of Access Act request, including a July 23 letter refusing to issue the company a license. A separate Sept. 25 letter extended its billing privileges through midnight Oct. 13, provided the company helps residents transfer to licensed providers.

"Law Enforcement responded to a call on September 13th, 2024, at 15 Autumn Ln, Brewer, after two different staff slapped a resident who refused to get out of a car," the notice states.
The letter does not identify the arrested workers or describe the outcome of their cases. The letter does not indicate whether those individuals continued to work for the company or found similar work at another autism company.
In addition to the death and violence, state investigators found We Care utterly disregarded practically ever rule for certifying that employees were competent, trained, and qualified to provide specialized care for high-need individuals.
A February 2026 found that "44 of 62 learners engaged in [Direct Support Professional] training through We Care, LLC completed this training in impossible timeframes, which led to the conclusion that the learning management system was manipulated to enable falsification of credentials," DHHS wrote.
DSP stands for direct support professional. The notice does not identify who manipulated the system or name the workers whose credentials were implicated.
Inspectors also found employees who could not demonstrate that they understood their training. The state letters do not say whether this lack of understanding was the result of employees inability to communicate in English -- the language spoken by 100% of their disabled patients.
At a separate home in Bangor, DHHS found "staff failed to demonstrate a fundamental understanding of Direct Support Professional (DSP) training, highlighting an inability to provide safe care for vulnerable residents in conformity with the MaineCare Benefits manual."
"Non-certified staff administered medications on five occasions in March 2026," the department wrote.
Under the MaineCare rules, staff must undergo background checks, immigration checks, and obtain DSP credentials before an agency can bill for their work. However, DHHS investigators found that We Care was systematically subverting the screening process and placing unqualified workers in autism group homes.
The deficiencies extended to the criminal background checks meant to screen employees before they began working with residents.
"33 of 33 new hires did not have a criminal background check done prior to date of hire," DHHS wrote, citing a May 2025 review.
That same review found that "27 of 33 workers did not have an Adult protective check prior to Date of Hire" and "32 of 33 newly hired workers did not have a Child Protective Services check done prior to the date of hire," according to the notice.
Emergency-response credentials were also missing or had gaps.
"15 of 33 workers did not have a valid Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR)/First Aid (FA) certificate for the entire fiscal year," the department wrote of the May review.
The January 2026 audit documented more certification failures.
"41 of 110 workers did not have a valid Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR)/First Aid (FA) certificate for the entire review period," DHHS wrote.

The notice lists "Medication errors including incorrect date of administration, failure to verify indication for prescribed medication and discontinued medication stored with current medication."

DHHS also rejected the possibility of granting the company a conditional license.
"DLC additionally concludes that licensing [We Care Residential] would not serve the best interests of the public and therefore a conditional license is not appropriate," the department wrote.
The funding termination followed in a separate process.

The letter does not indicate whether those individuals continued to work for the company or found similar work at another autism company. In addition to the death and violence, state investigators found We Care utterly disregarded practically ever rule for certifying that employees were competent, trained, and qualified to provide specialized care for high-need individuals. A February 2026 found that "44 of 62 learners engaged in [Direct Support Professional] training through We Care, LLC completed this training in impossible timeframes, which led to the conclusion that the learning management system was manipulated to enable falsification of credentials," DHHS wrote. DSP stands for direct support professional. The notice does not identify who manipulated the system or name the workers whose credentials were implicated. Inspectors also found employees who could not demonstrate that they understood their training. The state letters do not say whether this lack of understanding was the result of employees inability to communicate in English -- the language spoken by 100% of their disabled patients. At a separate home in Bangor, DHHS found "staff failed to demonstrate a fundamental understanding of Direct Support Professional (DSP) training, highlighting an inability to provide safe care for vulnerable residents in conformity with the MaineCare Benefits manual." "Non-certified staff administered medications on five occasions in March 2026," the department wrote. Under the MaineCare rules, staff must undergo background checks, immigration checks, and obtain DSP credentials before an agency can bill for their work. However, DHHS investigators found that We Care was systematically subverting the screening process and placing unqualified workers in autism group homes. The deficiencies extended to the criminal background checks meant to screen employees before they began working with residents. "33 of 33 new hires did not have a criminal background check done prior to date of hire," DHHS wrote, citing a May 2025 review. That same review found that "27 of 33 workers did not have an Adult protective check prior to Date of Hire" and "32 of 33 newly hired workers did not have a Child Protective Services check done prior to the date of hire," according to the notice. Emergency-response credentials were also missing or had gaps. "15 of 33 workers did not have a valid Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR)/First Aid (FA) certificate for the entire fiscal year," the department wrote of the May review. The January 2026 audit documented more certification failures. "41 of 110 workers did not have a valid Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR)/First Aid (FA) certificate for the entire review period," DHHS wrote. The audit also found that "34 of 82 reported workers that administer medication were missing a Certified Residential Medication Aide (CRMA) certificate and/or were missing a certificate for part of the review period," according to the notice. Even the qualifications of employees transporting residents were in question. "19 of 83 reported drivers did not have a valid license for part of the review period," the notice states. At We Care's New Gloucester home, the department documented repeated failures to supervise residents, including an incident months before the Brewer death. "Law enforcement discovered resident sitting in the road in Falmouth, several miles away from Resident's home," DHHS wrote of a March 3, 2024, incident. "Law enforcement returned to the residence and awoke [We Care Residential] staff to inform them of the elopement," the department wrote. The workers apparently did not know the resident had left. "[We Care Residential] staff informed Law Enforcement that Resident was still in their bedroom," the notice states. Nearly two years later, state inspectors encountered conditions that prompted them to leave the New Gloucester home. "DLC observed the residence to be in poor condition and left abruptly due to compromised safety from insufficient staff oversight," DHHS wrote of a Jan. 8, 2026, visit. (DLC is the department's Division of Licensing and Certification.) An investigation closed in March documented another resident leaving without staff noticing. "Three staff on duty were not aware that resident had eloped," the department wrote. During an April inspection attempt, employees failed to provide supervision even after state personnel specifically asked them to do so. "DLC team asked three [We Care Residential] staff to ensure supervision of the Resident during survey which staff failed to provide," the notice states. Inspectors also found medication problems at the Brewer house where the resident had died. ? The notice lists "Medication errors including incorrect date of administration, failure to verify indication for prescribed medication and discontinued medication stored with current medication." The department's conclusion was sweeping. "DLC concludes that [We Care Residential] has failed to provide adequate staffing to meet the needs of its residents, failed to ensure their staff have met training requirements, failed to administer and store medication in a safe manner, and failed to protect its residents from neglect," the July letter states. DHHS also rejected the possibility of granting the company a conditional license. "DLC additionally concludes that licensing [We Care Residential] would not serve the best interests of the public and therefore a conditional license is not appropriate," the department wrote. The funding termination followed in a separate process. It's not clear why We Care Residential was allowed to bill more than $6.5 million through 2024 and 2025 while inspection after inspection found glaring deficiencies, in addition to an assault and a death stemming from negligence. No We Care Residential staff have been charged with fraud or conspiracy as a result of the multi-year, multi-home scheme, and DHHS has not indicated whether it will seek to recoup money paid to We Care or seize properties owned by Rukumbuzi and Ndutira. With the termination of payments to We Care and Quality Care Access, Maine DHHS has now cutoff four autism group home operators this year, including Paradise Residential Services and Beyond Residential Care. Hey friends,
This one's a triple feature. Meet three Tennessee Democrats stepping up to run in this upcoming November election who couldn't be more different, and couldn't be more ready to challenge Tennessee’s status quo.
[**[CLICK HERE TO LISTEN NOW**](https://us.list-manage.com/z4Dwv6SsJxR?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0)]

[**Listen or watch**](https://us.list-manage.com/t7zImwMKTr1?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0)**now wherever you get your podcasts. 🎧**

[ Victoria Broderick](https://us.list-manage.com/3gzSYcGU7tc?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0) is taking on a Congressional District 4 incumbent so quiet I couldn't remember the last time I heard his name.
[Dr. Laura Andreson](https://us.list-manage.com/HZ27NZr41TN?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0), a 24-year OB-GYN, told me she felt she needed to hire a criminal defense attorney just to safely practice medicine under Tennessee's abortion laws — now she's running for TN House District 63.
[ Lindsey Patrick-Wright](https://us.list-manage.com/15kRSi93HtU?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0), a public librarian in Wilson County, decided book bans and bad leadership were reason enough to run for TN Senate District 17.
We cover cost-of-living pressures on working families, the real math behind school vouchers, book banning, and what's giving each of these women hope heading into the November 2026 election.

**Register to vote or check your voter registration**[**here**](https://us.list-manage.com/O_tIiJzp4DX?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0)**!****Confirm your district and look up your candidates**[**here**](https://us.list-manage.com/18G_orDx7wq?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0)**.**
**Dates to Remember:****Voter Registration Deadline:** Monday, October 5, 2026**Early Voting:** Wednesday, October 14 – Thursday, October 29, 2026**Absentee Ballot Request Deadline:** Saturday, October 24, 2026**Election Day:** Tuesday, November 3, 2026
We have real options in this election and I hope that you’ll take the time to learn more about these candidates or the ones running in your district.
Thank you for being here,
Gloria

# **Dept of Ed formally rescinds Biden-era Title IX rules, defines sex as male/female**
The Education Department finalized a rule Tuesday **[removing Biden-era Title IX regulations,](https://substack.com/redirect/fa5ce1ab-5f49-4f1f-981a-3b5cdba345e7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** which had extended protections based on gender identity and sexual orientation, and restoring Trump's first-term rules defining sex as male or female at birth.

---|---|---
* **A federal court struck down the 2024 rules in January 2025,** and the department has enforced 2020-era rules since; Monday's action formally updates the federal regulations after the last related lawsuits were dismissed in August.
* **Education Secretary Linda McMahon said the change aligns written regulations with court rulings** and current enforcement, framing it as reducing confusion while reaffirming protections for women's athletic and privacy rights.

# **Minnesota 's fraud problem just gets worse**

---|---|---
* **Policy analyst Bill Glahn, who previously scrutinized the city 's violence-interrupter program, said** grant recipients often lacked financial capacity or track records matching their funding, noting one participating organization had staffers involved in a violent incident in 2021.
* **The findings add to broader scrutiny of Minnesota 's fraud oversight following scandals in programs like Feeding Our Future.** The audit didn't identify specific fraud cases but warned of heightened risk; a city spokesperson said Minneapolis has since taken steps to improve contract oversight processes.

Hi, we’ll get straight to the point: We’re just 24 hours away from our End-of-Quarter deadline, so we have to ask: [**Will you pitch in any amount to help Sharice crush her September fundraising goal before Wednesday at midnight? This is the LAST End-of-Quarter fundraising deadline before Election Day, so your donation has never been more important.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140213827/649888822/-1547774912?refcode=email_092926_notice&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDIvMS82NTc1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkOWM0N2QwZi0xNWJjLWYxMTEtYTZhOS0wMDBkM2E1NmQyZjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=PnqoFc4cHhvwYUKax5oni5AbBFBS42hnrJA1gePWJeA=) Sharice represents the last blue dot in Kansas, which means National Republicans are keeping an _extremely_ close eye on this campaign. Every move we make, every fundraising email we send ahead of tomorrow night’s FEC deadline — they might as well be breathing down our necks! And we’ll be honest: It’s kind of annoying. But it also gives us a great idea. Right now, we’re still tracking $9,583 behind where we need to be. So if we make THIS email the one that helps us close that gap, National Republicans will notice immediately — and they’ll know Sharice has a strong grassroots team behind her, ready to step up and fight back. Because when our numbers go public next month, everyone — including our opponents — will be looking to see whether this campaign has the strength and momentum to hold KS-03. They’ll pull up our report the second it’s public. They’ll see how much we raised, how many people gave, and how much we have left to spread our message far and wide across the district with just 35 days to go. And then, they’ll decide how hard to come after us in this final stretch. And we’re not going to give them any opening. [**If we blow past our goal in the next 24 hours, National Republicans will know the momentum is on our side. So please: Rush $25 today. Case File No DRT-0929-A · The Regime Open
Every Tripwire Went Off Yesterday. This Morning, Tehran Says the Talks Covered No Details.
Oil +4%, a 19-year yield high and tech at the bottom of the board: all four of Monday’s tripwires tripped. Now Iran says its Qatar meeting was a handover, not a negotiation, and the ball is in Washington’s court.
Threat level 4/5 — Elevated
| | | | | | | | |
---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---
|
---
Yesterday we gave you four tripwires. All four went off. Oil jumped more than 4%, the 10-year hit its highest level since 2007, tech closed at the bottom of the board, and Iran confirmed it met Qatar’s mediators. Then this morning Tehran said the meeting covered no details at all. First, the scorecard.
Scorecard
| | Last Call: Did We Get It Right?
---|---
Sunday, Sept. 27
**Our call:** Watch whether the 10-year sets a fifth straight multi-decade high.
**What happened:** It did. The 10-year closed Monday at 5.243%, its highest since June 2007. The 30-year hit 5.560%, its highest since 2004.
| HIT
---
Monday, Sept. 28
**Our call:** Qatar’s mediators would meet the two sides early this week.
**What happened:** Confirmed on the record. Araghchi says Iran met Qatari mediators Monday at the UN General Assembly.
| HIT
---
Monday, Sept. 28
**Our call:** The AI agent story, not Iran, was doing most of the work in the Nasdaq’s drop.
**What happened:** Half right. Tech still closed worst (Nasdaq −0.92% vs. Dow −0.67%), but the gap shrank from nearly 3x to about 1.4x once oil’s 4% spike hit everything. Nvidia even rose 2.6%.
| PARTIAL
---

| | 4 for 4. Every One Went Off.
---|---

| | ✓

Tech underperforms the Dow at the close. **Tripped, barely:** −0.92% vs. −0.67%.
The evidence board
| | What Crossed the Desk
---|---
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit A — Tehran’s denial.** Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei: “No discussions regarding the details of the issues took place, and all media reports in this regard are merely speculation with no basis in reality.” Per Baghaei, Iran conveyed its positions and received Qatar’s “assessments.”
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit B — the ball.** Araghchi says Iran is now awaiting an official U.S. response through the same Qatari channel. Its conditions stand: an end to regional conflicts, a halt to U.S. strikes, the naval blockade lifted, and an arrangement for Hormuz.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit C — the lab.** OpenAI’s preparedness lead Micah Carroll: “All inference for our most capable models remains stopped until we have hardened our systems further.” No end date. In Asia, SK Hynix fell 4.8% and Samsung 4.6%; Taiwan’s market was shut for a holiday. In the U.S., ARM fell 8.7% and Intel 5.7%.
| CHATTER
---
**Exhibit D — the rumor.** Per a Wall Street Journal report relayed by Bloomberg, OpenAI scrapped its latest model release over safety fears. We could not verify the details; OpenAI has not confirmed it on the record.
| OUR THEORY
---
Monday’s meeting was a delivery, not a negotiation. Each side handed over its position and Qatar handed back its read. Oil’s 4% jump says traders read it the same way. The next real event is a U.S. reply, and Washington hasn’t said when one is coming.

Hi – Pete Buttigieg here.
Chris is running for U.S. Senate in New Hampshire, where I've had the opportunity to join on the trail and support his campaign. I've also worked with Chris on efforts to bring infrastructure investments and economic opportunity to communities across his state.
What stands out to me is not just Chris’s ability to get things done but the way he does it – listening carefully, communicating clearly, and staying relentlessly focused on delivering results for the people he serves.
**[Democrats have no chance of taking back the majority without holding New Hampshire’s seat. If you’re with me and ready to do everything we can to get Chris Pappas elected to the Senate, chip in $5 or whatever makes sense for you today.](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260929_1.NkOVtv&refcode=em20260929-1&t=2&akid=9202%2E582294%2En7emyj)**

There is a historic dimension at stake here too. If elected, Chris would become the first out gay man ever elected to the United States Senate. That representation matters, especially at a moment when so many Americans are wondering whether there’s still room in public life to live authentically and serve effectively at the same time.
But Chris isn’t running just because his campaign could make history. He’s running to do the job – to solve problems, lower costs, strengthen communities, and represent New Hampshire with seriousness and integrity in a very divided Washington.
And the reality is that control of the Senate could come down to just a handful of races. New Hampshire is one of them.
That means millions in outside spending, relentless attacks, and a long campaign ahead. Chris is going to need a strong grassroots team behind him every step of the way.

That representation matters, especially at a moment when so many Americans are wondering whether there’s still room in public life to live authentically and serve effectively at the same time. But Chris isn’t running just because his campaign could make history. He’s running to do the job – to solve problems, lower costs, strengthen communities, and represent New Hampshire with seriousness and integrity in a very divided Washington. And the reality is that control of the Senate could come down to just a handful of races. New Hampshire is one of them. That means millions in outside spending, relentless attacks, and a long campaign ahead. Chris is going to need a strong grassroots team behind him every step of the way. I’ve always believed that the best public service starts with listening, treating people with respect, communicating honestly, and staying focused on the work that matters most in people’s everyday lives. That’s the kind of leadership Chris has brought to the House, and it’s exactly what he’ll bring to the Senate. Thank you, Pete New Hampshire is poised to be one of the closest Senate races in the country. Will you chip in today to help Chris stop the Republicans from flipping the Granite State red and expanding their Senate majority?

name: Jeff Bridges
subject: From a hole in the ground to 54 homes
body:
Today I put my hand on a building that would not exist without a bill I passed. I don’t quite know how to describe how rewarding it felt.

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/08a7801e2b61/get-more-smarter-on-colorados-budget-10379097?e=b48bb2b4f4)
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/yZkWav522Cy?e=b48bb2b4f4&c2id=bbe572662fdb5fed2d0855c1bcb00da8)
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | Hi there,
Last year, I broke ground in Frisco on a new workforce housing project called The Scout. Today, I came back and cut the ribbon. Not much more than a hole in the ground last year is now 54 homes for people living and working in Summit County.
---
|
---
| | It took Frisco, Summit County, the Department of Local Affairs, the NHP Foundation, and Colorado’s Middle-Income Housing Authority to get it built. That last one, MIHA, is the authority I created back in 2022 through the hardest legislative fight of my ten years in office.

Weeks of drafting. Emails back and forth at all hours of the night negotiating more than 60 amendments. Getting stuck. Finding a path forward. Getting stuck again.
**Today I put my hand on a building that would not exist without that work. I don’t quite know how to describe how rewarding it felt. Teachers. First responders. Nurses. Town employees. People who keep their community running now have a home they can afford.**
---
|
---
| | Housing costs, especially in our mountain communities, have gotten so high that people who work there often can’t afford to live there. Most make too much to qualify for traditional low-income housing, but nowhere near enough to afford market rents.
**That’s exactly the gap Scout was built to fill.**
Those late night drafting sessions didn’t build The Scout on their own. A whole lot of other people made that happen. And there's a lot more housing we need to build in Colorado, especially in places where the people we depend on can't afford to live.
And that's what I plan to work on as Treasurer—building more homes like the Scout.
---
| | Talk soon,
ps This weekend we're hitting the road with Phil and Joe! Stay tuned!

| | Moms have an important role in protecting and guiding our children, and sometimes that starts with simply knowing what they’re facing. On this episode of the Moms for America Podcast, Debbie Kraulidis talks with Penny Nance, President and CEO of Concerned Women for America, about standing strong for our families, biblical values, and the challenges facing moms today. Iran Denied the Details, Not the Meeting. That’s the Tell.
Tehran calls reports on its Qatar talks ‘baseless speculation’ while confirming it handed over its position and now waits on Washington. OpenAI says its best models stay offline ‘until’ — no date given. Three statements, decoded.
Threat level 4/5 — Elevated
| | | | | | | | |
---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---
|
---
Three statements since Monday, from two governments and one AI lab. All three are careful about what they leave out. Here’s what each one says, what it gives away, and who is now holding which card.
Decoder · Line 01
| | A Denial That Confirms the Channel
---|---
| | “No discussions regarding the details of the issues took place, and all media reports in this regard are merely speculation with no basis in reality.”— Esmaeil Baghaei, Iran Foreign Ministry spokesman
---|---
What it says
The reports about what was discussed with Qatar are false.
What it means
**Our theory:** read what is denied. Baghaei rejects the _content_ of the reports, not the meeting. Iran confirms it sent its positions and got Qatar’s “assessments” back. Tehran’s reason is simple: any leaked detail would look like a concession at home. So the channel is working. It’s just being kept quiet.
Decoder · Line 02
| | The Ball, Formally Handed Over
---|---
| EVIDENCE
---
Per Iranian state media, Araghchi told reporters Iran held another meeting with Qatari intermediaries on Monday and is now awaiting an official U.S. response through the same channel. Its conditions are unchanged.
| OUR THEORY
---
This makes the weekend’s “your move” posture official. Once Iran has formally delivered its position through a mediator, every day without a U.S. answer is Washington’s choice, on the record. Tehran is building a paper trail aimed at Qatar, Europe and oil buyers as much as at the White House.
Decoder · Line 03
| | A Pause With No Clock
---|---
| | “All inference for our most capable models remains stopped until we have hardened our systems further.”— Micah Carroll, OpenAI preparedness lead
---|---
What it says
OpenAI’s strongest models stay offline until security is fixed.
What it means
**Our theory:** the key word is “until.” No date, no milestone, no criteria in public. The chip market is struggling to price exactly that. A pause with an end date is a delay. A pause without one is an open question about the AI buildout, and SK Hynix, Samsung, ARM and Intel all traded Monday as if it’s an open question.
The board
| | Who’s Holding Which Card
---|---
| | YOUR MOVE
---
Washington
Now formally owes a reply through Qatar. Hasn’t said whether or when one is coming. Holds the blockade and the calendar card: the midterms.
| | WAITING
---
Tehran
Delivered its position and says its conditions are unchanged. Denies any details were discussed, which keeps its hand hidden.
| | DELIVERING
---
Doha
Carried both sides’ positions and handed back its own “assessments.” Whatever those were, they’re the most valuable document nobody has seen.
| | PAUSED
---
OpenAI
Stopped its most capable models with no restart date, and possibly shelved a release. The one player whose next move nobody can force.
Still blacked out
| | What We Can’t See Yet
---|---
| ██ REDACTED ██
---
What Qatar’s “assessments” said. That’s the only new document created on Monday, and neither side has described it.
| ██ REDACTED ██
---
Whether Washington has drafted a reply at all, or is running out the clock to November as reported last week.
| ██ REDACTED ██
---
Whether OpenAI actually scrapped a model release. So far that rests on a single WSJ report relayed by Bloomberg.
| ClassificationPressure
---
The diplomatic channel works, and everyone is keeping it quiet. The next concrete event, a U.S. reply, has no date. Until it arrives, markets will keep pricing the silence: oil up, yields up.

name: Caroline Welles
subject: 📎Enclosed: An important ask for you
body:
Can we get your help to elect progressive women?
#
I’m Caroline Welles, founder of The First Ask. You are someone who cares about sending progressives to office, so I wanted to reach out to ask you to be a part of something today.
Let me ask you a question: _Have you been happy with how things have been going in our politics lately?_
HA, kind of a trick question, right? Is anybody?
The federal government has been a mess. Congress is pure chaos. The Senate has practically ground to a halt. Don’t get me started on the White House.
**Here’s why The First Ask exists: to identify, elevate, and fund Democratic women running for state legislature in the districts where every vote counts.** We believe in power from the ground up. And this political moment has proven just how important that state-level power is in protecting us from the corruption and chaos at the national level. (If you’re already sold on this mission, [**you can support it here**](https://act.leftnet.org/go/21583?c0=tfa_leftnet.2zy7vx&refcode=em20260929-1717&t=1&akid=1717%2E2118727%2EeZobGb).)
[](https://act.leftnet.org/go/21583?c0=tfa_leftnet.2zy7vx&refcode=em20260929-1717&t=2&akid=1717%2E2118727%2EeZobGb)
Our state reps decide what happens to our public schools. Women’s access to healthcare and their reproductive freedoms. Whether families can afford to stay in the communities they call home. Whether a data center will swoop in and suck up a neighborhood's land, water, and power before anyone even realizes what just happened.
And in some of the most competitive districts in the country, a handful of votes could decide which party gets to make those decisions.**
**
**Today, I'm reaching out to ask you to be a part of this mission. We are in this work for the long haul, not just one election. But right now we have candidates who need our help, with state house majorities on the line. If you’re ready to jump into this fight,[can you chip in $10 to help us fund these campaigns all the way to November? Your donation will go right back to work helping to elect progressive Democratic women who actually care about the issues you and I care about.](https://act.leftnet.org/go/22104?c0=tfa_leftnet.Nr4z13&refcode=em20260929-1717&t=3&akid=1717%2E2118727%2EeZobGb)**
**[DONATE $10 ››](https://act.leftnet.org/go/22104?c0=tfa_leftnet.Nr4z13&refcode=em20260929-1717&t=4&akid=1717%2E2118727%2EeZobGb)**
**[DONATE OTHER ››](https://act.leftnet.org/go/21583?c0=tfa_leftnet.2zy7vx&refcode=em20260929-1717&t=5&akid=1717%2E2118727%2EeZobGb)**
**I know $10 might seem small. But in races that come down to a few dozen votes, it isn't.**
Donations that come in now let us move fast: plan, support our candidates, and put resources where they'll make the difference in the final weeks before they win.
It's officially election season, and for our candidates it's time to knock doors, make phone calls, buy ad space, and get voters ready to cast their ballots. All of that takes dollars in the door, and we want to be able to support this work every step of the way to Election Day.
[**Your $10 today puts resources behind candidates fighting at the state level for lower costs, our rights, and our future, in battleground districts, during the most important stretch of their campaigns. Will you chip in and show your support today?**](https://act.leftnet.org/go/22104?c0=tfa_leftnet.Nr4z13&refcode=em20260929-1717&t=6&akid=1717%2E2118727%2EeZobGb)
I’m so glad you’re part of this team now. We can do this together.
— Caroline

**LeftNet is an online political network fighting for progressive causes and candidates focused on social, racial, economic, and environmental justice.**
---
